name: Efficient LLM Adapter Fine-Tuning Pipeline Template
summary: Reusable base CDG for LLM efficiency, model adaptation, instruction tuning, and resource-constrained fine-tuning competitions that combine curated prompt data, distillation or quality filtering, LoRA/QLoRA or LoRA-MoE adapters, memory-efficient training controls such as FlashAttention-2, bf16, gradient accumulation, paged optimizers, and adapter routing or merge-time calibration.
dejargonized_summary: Prepare filtered instruction or prompt data, fine-tune a large language model through lightweight adapters such as LoRA, QLoRA, or LoRA-MoE, use memory-saving training controls so the model fits on available hardware, optionally route or merge task adapters, and calibrate outputs for the benchmark metric.

inputs.name: instruction_or_prompt_data
inputs.constraints: Prompts, instructions, responses, preference labels, or task examples.

outputs.name: fine_tuned_llm_outputs
outputs.constraints: Generated answers, scores, labels, or adapter artifacts formatted for the benchmark metric.

use_when: The solution is dominated by adapting a pretrained LLM under memory, speed, or parameter-budget constraints.

Winning techniques include LoRA, QLoRA, LoRA-MoE, adapter routing, FlashAttention-2, paged optimizers, bf16, gradient accumulation, EWC, data distillation, curated Open-Orca style instruction data, or synthetic self-play examples.
The task requires model training or adapter selection rather than only prompt engineering or shallow cross-encoder scoring.
do_not_use_when: The task is classic text-pair matching with handcrafted lexical features and no LLM fine-tuning.
The task is LLM preference ranking where the key topology is paired response scoring rather than efficient adapter training.
The task can be solved with static embeddings, tabular models, or retrieval without updating model weights.
applicability.key_insight: The durable topology is adapter-based model adaptation under explicit resource controls. This is separate from generic LLM preference CDGs because memory layout, quantization, optimizer choice, and adapter routing are load-bearing stages.

swappable_stages.adapter_initialization: Can use LoRA, QLoRA, LoRA-MoE, IA3, prefix tuning, or task-specific adapters if the adapted weights remain parameter-efficient.
swappable_stages.memory_efficient_training: Can use FlashAttention-2, gradient checkpointing, paged optimizers, bf16/fp16, quantized base weights, or gradient accumulation.
swappable_stages.data_curation_distillation: Can use quality filtering, teacher distillation, Open-Orca style instruction data, synthetic self-play, or hard-example mining.

applicability.scaling_notes: Cache tokenization, keep sequence-length policy fixed before training, validate memory controls on the target hardware, and evaluate adapter merges on held-out prompts.
failure_modes: Low-quality distilled data can degrade adapters even when training loss improves.
Changing quantization, precision, or sequence length between validation and final training can shift results.
Adapter routing can overfit task IDs or prompt templates if validation is not split-aware.

planning_constraints.subject: curation_before_adapter_training
planning_constraints.statement: Filter, distill, or construct instruction data before adapter initialization and training.
planning_constraints.rationale: Adapter updates inherit bias and noise from the training examples; training controls cannot recover from poor data curation.

planning_constraints.subject: memory_policy_before_training
planning_constraints.statement: Fix quantization, attention implementation, precision, optimizer paging, gradient accumulation, and checkpointing before model selection.
planning_constraints.rationale: The feasible batch size and context length determine the adapter training regime and can change model quality.

audit.rationale: Added after validation left repeated divergent LLM efficiency and LLM fine-tuning solutions whose missing techniques were QLoRA, LoRA-MoE, FlashAttention-2, paged optimizers, bf16, gradient accumulation, data distillation, EWC, adapter routing, and curated instruction tuning. Semantic comparison found the existing LLM preference reasoning topology too focused on prompt-pair scoring and preference heads.
audit.dejargonized_summary: This covers competitions where the main reusable operation is memory-efficient fine-tuning of a pretrained language model with adapters.
uncertainty_notes: Preference-head and prompt-pair techniques remain in llm_preference_reasoning_topology; this CDG should stay focused on adapter training and resource policy.

references.title: Sciona 132-CDG expansion validation audit
references.note: Local deterministic and semantic audit of unmatched efficient LLM fine-tuning patterns.

stages.name: Data Curation and Distillation
stages.description: Filter noisy prompt-response data, select high-quality instruction examples, add teacher-distilled responses, Open-Orca style instruction data, synthetic self-play examples, or hard examples.
stages.dejargonized_description: Build a clean training set before updating the language model.

inputs.name: instruction_or_prompt_data
inputs.constraints: Raw prompt, instruction, response, or label data.

preconditions: Raw examples and split policy are available.
guarantees: Training data provenance and validation boundaries are explicit.

stages.name: Adapter Initialization
stages.description: Attach LoRA, QLoRA, LoRA-MoE, prefix, or task-specific adapters to a pretrained LLM, including 4-bit quantized base weights when needed.
stages.dejargonized_description: Add small trainable modules to a pretrained language model instead of updating every weight.

outputs.name: adapter_training_plan
outputs.constraints: Backbone, tokenizer, adapter, and quantization policy.

preconditions: Backbone model, tokenizer, and adapter rank policy are selected.

stages.name: Memory-Efficient Training
stages.description: Train adapters with FlashAttention-2, bf16/fp16 mixed precision, gradient accumulation, paged optimizers, gradient checkpointing, quantized 4-bit weights, and sequence-length controls.
stages.dejargonized_description: Fine-tune the model while staying inside memory and runtime limits.

outputs.name: trained_adapters
outputs.constraints: Fine-tuned adapter weights and training logs.

preconditions: Hardware budget and validation split are fixed.
guarantees: Training uses the declared memory policy.

stages.name: Adapter Routing or Merging
stages.description: Route task examples through specialized adapters, merge adapters, apply LoRA-MoE gating, or use EWC to retain prior capabilities across tasks.
stages.dejargonized_description: Choose or combine the trained adapters for each task or prompt type.
preconditions: Adapter selection or merge policy is known.
guarantees: Inference uses the intended adapter path.

stages.name: Metric Calibration
stages.description: Tune decoding, thresholds, rank aggregation, validation checkpoints, or adapter merge weights against the benchmark metric.
stages.dejargonized_description: Convert adapted model outputs into the exact final format required by the competition.
preconditions: Metric and submission format are known.
guarantees: Outputs are calibrated and formatted for submission.
